scenes.text: Saturn is the only planet in our solar system that's less dense than water.
It's about nine times wider than Earth, but it's made mostly of light hydrogen and helium gas.
On average, it's only about seven tenths as dense as water.
That's why NASA jokes that Saturn could float in a bathtub, if one were big enough.
In reality, it wouldn't bob like a rubber duck, because it has no solid surface to hold it together.
But no other planet even comes close to being that light for its size.

title: Saturn is lighter than water 🪐
caption: Saturn's average density is about 0.69 g/cm³, lower than water's 1 g/cm³, the only planet like that. NASA says it could float in a big enough bathtub, though it would really fall apart. 🪐
